basicPropertyValues.val: A DCAT Profile for Data Access, Storage and Authorization Metadata.
QUAY: Qualified Usage, Access and Yield

definition.val: Qualification node that specifies how a distribution is reached, comprising exactly one protocol, at least one authentication scheme, and at least one supported operation.

comments: Qualifies HOW a Distribution is reached.

definition.val: Encryption using the Advanced Encryption Standard with a 128-bit key.
Encryption using the Advanced Encryption Standard with a 256-bit key.
Authentication scheme that verifies identity by presenting a pre-shared secret key with each request.
Temporal quality in which data is preserved for long-term retention and is no longer actively updated.
Method used to verify the identity of an agent requesting access to a data resource.
Authentication scheme that verifies identity using an AWS access key identifier and secret access key pair.
Authentication scheme that verifies identity by transmitting a username and password pair, typically Base64-encoded.
Service quality in which availability depends on upstream network and server conditions without formal guarantees.

comments: Quality depends on upstream server or network conditions.

definition.val: Protocol that distributes data across a swarm of peers using piece-based transfer and a distributed hash table for coordination.
Delivery mode in which data is transferred as a complete unit within a single transaction.
Coverage in which the distribution contains the entirety of the available data of its dataset.
Verification method in which data is both identified and verified by a hash derived from its content, such that the identifier itself proves integrity.

comments: Content identified and verified by its hash, as in IPFS CIDs.

definition.val: Characterisation of the extent to which a distribution represents the total available data of a dataset.
Operation that permanently removes data from a data resource.
Mechanism by which data is transferred from a data resource to a consuming agent.
Verification method that confirms both integrity and authenticity of data by validating a cryptographic signature produced by a known key holder.

comments: Integrity and authenticity verified via cryptographic signature.

definition.val: Service quality in which data is replicated across multiple independent nodes for fault tolerance.

comments: Data distributed across multiple peers or nodes.

definition.val: Cryptographic algorithm or protocol used to protect data confidentiality, either at rest or in transit.
Delivery mode in which data transfer is triggered by the occurrence of discrete events or state changes.
Protocol that transfers files between client and server using the File Transfer Protocol.
Protocol that accesses version-controlled data through the Git distributed version control system.
Encryption using GNU Privacy Guard, an implementation of the OpenPGP standard.
Authentication scheme that verifies identity and enables data signing using a GNU Privacy Guard key pair.
Verification method that confirms data integrity by computing a cryptographic hash of the received content and comparing it against a known reference value.

comments: Integrity verified by comparing cryptographic hash of content.

definition.val: Service quality in which the service is operated with infrastructure redundancy and contractual uptime guarantees.

comments: Managed cloud services with SLA guarantees.

definition.val: Protocol that delegates data access operations to user-defined external scripts or commands.

comments: Custom protocol via user-defined hook scripts.

definition.val: Protocol that transfers data using the Hypertext Transfer Protocol, optionally secured with Transport Layer Security.
Coverage in which the distribution contains only changes accumulated since a specified reference point.
Protocol that addresses and retrieves data by cryptographic content identifier on the InterPlanetary File System network.
Operation that enumerates the available entries or contents of a data resource.
Protocol that accesses data directly through the operating system local filesystem interface without network transfer.
Authentication scheme that permits access without requiring identity verification.
Designation indicating that no encryption is applied to the data.
Verification method designation indicating that no integrity or authenticity verification mechanism is applied.
Authentication scheme that verifies identity through the OAuth 2.0 authorization framework using token-based delegated access.
Action that can be performed on a data resource through an access point.
Delivery mode in which data is transferred in discrete, sequentially ordered pages of bounded size.
Delivery mode in which data is transferred directly between participating peers without routing through a central server.
Verification method that confirms integrity of individual data segments by validating each against a Merkle hash tree.

comments: Integrity verified per-piece using a hash tree, as in BitTorrent.

definition.val: Communication method that governs the rules and format of data exchange between a client and a data resource.
Protocol that delegates data access to the rclone tool, which abstracts over multiple cloud storage backends.
Operation that retrieves data from a data resource without modifying it.
Temporal quality in which data reflects the current state of its source with minimal latency.
Operation that copies data from one data resource to another for redundancy or distribution.
Protocol that synchronises files between locations using the rsync delta-transfer algorithm.
Protocol that accesses object storage using the Amazon Simple Storage Service API.
Coverage in which the distribution contains a statistically representative fraction of the available data.
Characterisation of the reliability, availability, and redundancy properties of a data access service.
Service quality in which data resides on a single machine with no infrastructure redundancy.

comments: Data resides on a single machine with no redundancy.

definition.val: Temporal quality in which data represents a consistent state captured at a specific point in time.
Encryption using the Secure Shell protocol for transport-layer data protection.
Authentication scheme that verifies identity using an asymmetric SSH key pair.
Protocol that provides encrypted file transfer and remote command execution over a Secure Shell connection.
Delivery mode in which data is transferred as a continuous flow of incremental units over a persistent connection.
Coverage in which the distribution contains a defined, criteria-based portion of the available data.
Delivery mode in which data is transferred within a blocking request-response cycle that completes before control returns to the caller.
Characterisation of the freshness and currency of data available from a distribution.
Encryption using Transport Layer Security version 1.2 as specified in RFC 5246.
Encryption using Transport Layer Security version 1.3 as specified in RFC 8446.
Mechanism used to confirm the integrity or authenticity of data after transfer.
Temporal quality in which data is maintained as a sequence of immutable, individually identifiable revisions.
Protocol that extends HTTP with distributed authoring and versioning capabilities for remote file management.
Operation that stores new data in or modifies existing data within a data resource.
Qualification node that specifies what a distribution delivers, comprising exactly one delivery mode and optional temporal quality, coverage, service quality, and verification method descriptors.
Relates a distribution to a qualification node that describes how it is accessed.
Relates an access description to the method used to verify the identity of the accessing agent.
Relates a yield description to the extent of dataset representation in the distribution.
Relates a yield description to the mechanism by which data is transferred to the consumer.
Relates a distribution to the encryption algorithm applied to data at rest within the storage backend.
Relates a distribution to the encryption protocol applied to data during transfer between client and server.
Relates an access description to the communication protocol used for data exchange.
Relates a yield description to the reliability and availability characterisation of the service.
Relates a distribution to the legal jurisdiction or geographic region where data is physically stored.
Relates an access description to an action that can be performed on the data resource.
Relates a yield description to the freshness characterisation of the available data.
Relates a yield description to the mechanism used to verify data integrity after transfer.
Relates a distribution to a qualification node that describes what it delivers.
Human-readable description of the cost or pricing model for accessing the distribution.
Usage quota describing the maximum allowed consumption of the service.
Maximum number of requests permitted within a time window.
Maximum acceptable duration of data loss measured as a time window before the disruption.
Maximum acceptable duration to restore service after a disruption.
Number of independent copies of the data maintained across storage nodes.
Duration for which data is guaranteed to be retained before deletion or archival.
Percentage of time the service is operational and accessible, expressed as a decimal value between 0 and 100.
